plan.summary: Total IEEPA duty at stake is $243,524 principal plus $14,945 interest; $145,551 is reachable now through CAPE across 89 entries. $25,226 across 12 entries is urgent (soonest deadline in 3 days), $47,467 requires protests before 180‑day deadlines, and $32,499 is litigation‑only after 180 days.

steps.do: File CAPE for the 12 urgent entries ($25,226 total) before their 80‑day deadlines — first deadline is Oct 28 (entry Q7Z-4101104-9, $1,810).
steps.why: Importer or licensed broker via ACE

steps.do: Confirm your refund bank account with CBP; as of Oct 2 they were holding ~$1.1B in approved refunds for missing banking details.
File Post Summary Corrections for 2 entries (Q7Z-4103309-2 $3,247.50 and Q7Z-4103339-9 $2,450) before any CAPE filing — PSC is blocked once CAPE accepts.
Consult broker on 3 open protests (entries Q7Z-4103107-0, Q7Z-4103142-7, plus one other): if IEEPA‑only and within 80 days of liquidation, consider withdrawing to file CAPE; otherwise keep protest.
Address blocked items: notify surety on 2 surety‑paid entries (no CAPE process yet); monitor CBP guidance on 3 drawback entries; verify 3 entries where someone else holds the claim ($2,967).
Track 4 entries already on accepted CAPE declarations ($8,030 principal) via ACE reports ES-022/REV-603; prepare for 2027-02-01 court deadlines on 31 litigation entries ($32,499).

watch_outs: Missing bank account: CBP pays refunds only electronically — your $145,551 could sit in the ~$1.1B held for missing details.
Surety-paid entries: CBP says do not file these in CAPE; no surety refund process exists yet.
Open protests: CAPE rejects protested entries; withdrawing a protest risks losing non‑IEEPA grounds.
PSC timing: Corrections must be filed before CAPE acceptance; once CAPE accepts, a PSC can no longer be filed.

explanations.Q7Z-4103455-3: This AD/CVD suspended entry has $1,520 in principal plus $88.11 in interest tied up. File the refund request in CAPE now so the IEEPA duties come off, but the actual refund won’t be paid until Commerce lifts the suspension. No deadline is shown, so treat “now” as the practical cutoff. The uncertain part is when Commerce will lift the suspension — that timing controls when you actually get paid.
explanations.Q7Z-4103309-2: This entry requires a Post Summary Correction (PSC) to be filed and accepted before you can submit a CAPE claim for the IEEPA refund. You must file the PSC first—through your broker in ACE—then follow up with the CAPE filing; the PSC itself cannot claim the refund. No deadline or liquidation date is provided, so the timing is uncertain; act promptly to avoid missing any future cutoff. The rule carries a provisional confidence tag (P), meaning the guidance could be updated.
explanations.Q7Z-4101559-4: This entry liquidated on April 30, 2026, putting it 81–180 days past liquidation, so the CAPE refund path is not available today. You have **2 days (until October 27, 2026)** to file a protest in ACE to preserve your rights on the $1,567.50 principal plus $125.01 interest. After that, your main option is discussing a Court of International Trade case with counsel. The “P” confidence tag means this assessment is planning-level, not a guaranteed outcome.
explanations.K4M-9231751-6: This entry liquidated 81–180 days ago and you are not the importer of record, so the refund belongs to that party and no CAPE path is available today. To preserve any rights, file a protest in ACE before the 180‑day deadline on 2026‑12‑03 (39 days left) and/or consult counsel about a CIT case. The liquidation date (2026‑06‑06) is estimated from the entry date and must be confirmed in ACE before acting. Because the importer of record is not you, the $1,046 principal plus $76.58 interest are not yours to claim unless that importer assigns the right.
explanations.Q7Z-4102801-9: This entry contains only a $530 Section 122 surcharge, which cannot be refunded through the CAPE/IEEPA process. To preserve any future claim, you (or your broker) must file a protest under 19 U.S.C. § 1514(c)(3) within 180 days of the entry’s liquidation date. Because the liquidation date isn’t provided, the exact deadline is uncertain — ask your broker or counsel to confirm it and file the protest on time. No IEEPA refund is available for this entry.
explanations.Q7Z-4103107-0: Your entry has an open protest, and CAPE automatically rejects any protested entry — so the protest must be resolved before a refund can proceed. If the protest covers **only** the IEEPA duties and today is within 80 days of the 2026-06-25 liquidation date, you (or your broker) should withdraw the protest and file the CAPE claim; otherwise the protest stays in place. The critical unknowns are (1) whether the protest scope is limited to IEEPA and (2) whether you’re still inside that 80-day window — both need confirmation before acting.
explanations.Q7Z-4103424-9: Your warehouse entry (type 21/22) for $1,640 plus $69.31 interest can no longer be processed through CAPE because CBP stopped accepting that entry type on July 7, 2026. You must file withdrawal entries (types 31, 32, 34, or 38) instead to pursue any refund. No deadline appears in the data, so the timing is uncertain; the rule itself carries only a “P” confidence tag, meaning it may still be subject to change.
explanations.Q7Z-4101104-9: This entry liquidated on August 9, 2026, giving you until October 28, 2026 (80 days after liquidation) to file a CAPE refund claim for $1,810 in principal plus $115.34 in interest. You must file the claim in ACE yourself or through your licensed broker within the next 3 days, as CBP is required to accept it by the 80‑day deadline. The “P” confidence tag means the rule interpretation is provisional, so confirm eligibility with your broker, especially since the entry involves the India (Russian oil) and Reciprocal tariff programs. RefundRadar does not file claims; only you or your broker can submit in ACE.
